newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks erase slim loss, close higher.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks erase slim loss, close higher.

text.p: Argentine stocks soaked up a mild bout of profit-taking and closed firm Wednesday, resuming their upward course, dealers said.
"The market is heading for the 700 mark but it may push even higher thanks to momentum provided by next week's ($2.0 billion) global bond issue," said Jorge Bonanno at Interfin brokers.
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV tacked on 0.5 percent to close at 691.73, stretching Tuesday's 2.1 percent gain. It has advanced 6.5 percent so far in January and stands at a three-year high.

"What the bolsa did today was temper its bullish mood in keeping with a Wall Street pullback," said Bonanno. "But the AFJPs (private pension) funds were in there again building up positions, which eventually lured the smaller players back."
Traders said stocks were given a lift by the local goverment bonds market, which defied a drop in U.S. Treasuries and continued their recent rally.

"It's obvious everyone is feeling good about the global bond -- we're taking our cue from the fixed income market," said an analyst at another local brokerage. The bond deal, expected by Wednesday, offers five and 20-year maturities.
The bolsa's broad market index closed up 0.8 percent, with winners beating losers 39 to 22 and 23 stocks closing flat.
Floor volume shrank to 31.8 million pesos from Tuesday's strong tally of 38 million, while over-the-counter turnover picked up to 132 million pesos from 112 million Tuesday.
Top main-tier performers were carmaker Ciadea, which rose 4.5 percent, oil giant YPF and power utility Central Costanera, both up 2.1 percent, and Telecom, up 1.8 percent.
Heaviest losses were in oil company Astra, construction stock Polledo and foods giant Molinos, which shed 2.0 percent, 1.9 percent and 1.8 percent, respectively.
